derivations.claim: Order coordinates as $(E_1,n_1,\ldots,E_r,n_r)$. The first row of $A$ has $E_i$ coefficient $N_i>0$, while the second row has every $E_i$ coefficient zero and every $n_i$ coefficient one. Hence the two rows are linearly independent and $\operatorname{rank}A=2$. Therefore $\dim(\ker A)^\perp=2$. The range of $A^\mathsf T$ is contained in $(\ker A)^\perp$ because $A^\mathsf Ty\cdot h=y\cdot Ah=0$ whenever $h\in\ker A$; $A^\mathsf T$ is injective since $A$ has rank two. Its range also has dimension two, so $\operatorname{range}(A^\mathsf T)=(\ker A)^\perp$.

Under the forward hypothesis [A3], $
abla S_{m tot}(x^*)$ is orthogonal to $\ker A$, hence lies in $\operatorname{range}(A^\mathsf T)$ by step 1.1. Thus there are unique multipliers $\lambda,
u\in\mathbb R$ with, for each $i$,
$$\partial_{E_i}S_i(x_i^*)=\lambda N_i,\qquad \partial_{n_i}S_i(x_i^*)=\lambda q\Phi_i+
u.$$
Since $\partial_{E_i}S_i(x_i^*)>0$ and $N_i>0$, $\lambda>0$.

Under [A3], set $T_K:=1/\lambda>0$ and $\mu_K:=-
u/\lambda$ using the multipliers of step 2.1. The first multiplier equation gives $1/T_i=\lambda N_i$, so $N_iT_i=T_K$. The second gives $-\mu_i/T_i=\lambda q\Phi_i+
u$. Multiplying by $-N_iT_i$ and using $N_iT_i=1/\lambda$ yields $N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=-
u/\lambda=\mu_K$. Conversely, assume [A4] and set $\lambda:=1/T_K$ and $
u:=-\mu_K/T_K$. Then $\partial_{E_i}S_i(x_i^*)=1/T_i=N_i/T_K=\lambda N_i$, and $\partial_{n_i}S_i(x_i^*)=-\mu_i/T_i=-N_i\mu_i/T_K=(q\Phi_i-\mu_K)/T_K=\lambda q\Phi_i+
u$. Thus $
abla S_{m tot}(x^*)=A^\mathsf T(\lambda,
u)$. For every $h\in\ker A$, $DS_{m tot}(x^*)[h]=(\lambda,
u)\cdot Ah=0$; feasibility is [A2], so $x^*$ is stationary. This proves the reverse implication without using the forward stationarity hypothesis.

For the concavity conclusion assume [A3]. For any other feasible $y\in U$, $A(y-x^*)=0$. By step 2.1, $
abla S_{m tot}(x^*)=A^\mathsf T(\lambda,
u)$, hence $DS_{m tot}(x^*)[y-x^*]=0$. Put $\varphi(t):=S_{m tot}(x^*+t(y-x^*))$ for $0\le t\le1$. For $0<s<t\le1$, concavity gives $\varphi(s)\ge(1-s/t)\varphi(0)+(s/t)\varphi(t)$, so $(\varphi(s)-\varphi(0))/s\ge(\varphi(t)-\varphi(0))/t$. Letting $s\downarrow0$ and using differentiability shows $\varphi(t)-\varphi(0)\le t\varphi'(0)=0$, so $S_{m tot}(y)\le S_{m tot}(x^*)$. If every $S_i$ is strictly concave and $y
e x^*$, at least one cell coordinate differs; its entropy is strictly concave along the segment, while every other cell entropy is concave, so their sum $\varphi$ is strictly concave. If $y$ were also a maximizer, strict concavity would give $\varphi(t)>(1-t)\varphi(0)+t\varphi(1)=\varphi(0)$ for $0<t<1$, contradicting the tangent bound. Thus no distinct feasible $y$ is also a maximizer. This proves the conditional maximum and uniqueness claims without asserting that any stationary point exists.

Use SI dimensions and the signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Take the geometric data of
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]: $O$ is a nonempty connected open domain in a
smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$, $\nabla$ is the
Levi–Civita connection, and $\xi$ is a smooth future-directed timelike Killing
field with dimensionless components in physical length coordinates $x^0=ct$
and $x^i$ measured in metres. Put $N:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and
$u:=\xi/N$, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its smooth
tangent-bundle data carry the supplier's explicit foundational assumption
[[def-countable-choice]] ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$); no stronger choice principle
is added here.

For a smooth real one-form $A$ on $O$, define the electromagnetic two-form by
$$F_{ab}:=(dA)_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a.$$
Here $A_a$ has units tesla metres and $F_{ab}$ has units tesla. A global gauge
compensator is a smooth real function $\Lambda_\xi$ on $O$ satisfying
$$(\mathcal L_\xi A)_a:=\xi^b\partial_bA_a+A_b\partial_a\xi^b =\partial_a\Lambda_\xi.$$
The units of $\Lambda_\xi$ are tesla metres. Define contraction by
$(\iota_\xi F)_a:=\xi^bF_{ba}$ and set
$$\Psi_\xi:=\xi^aA_a-\Lambda_\xi,\qquad \Phi_\xi:=-c\Psi_\xi.$$
Thus $\Psi_\xi$ has units tesla metres and $\Phi_\xi$ has units volts.

Let $c>0$ be the speed of light, let $m>0$ be a particle rest mass in
kilograms, let $q\in\mathbb R$ be its charge in coulombs, and put
$M:=mc^2>0$ joules. A charged massive Lorentz trajectory is a $C^2$ curve
$x:J\to O$, where $J$ is an open real interval, parametrized by physical
length $s_m=c\tau$ in metres, with future unit tangent
$w:=dx/ds_m$, $g(w,w)=-1$, energy four-vector $P:=Mw$, and equation
$$\nabla_wP^a=cqF^a{}_bw^b,\qquad F^a{}_b:=g^{ac}F_{cb}.$$
In particular $g(P,P)=-M^2$ and $P$ is future directed. This is a conditional
definition of curves satisfying the equation; it makes no existence claim.

The future massive shell for this definition is the subset
$$\mathcal P_M^+(O):=\{(x,P)\in TO:g_x(P,P)=-M^2,\ P\text{ future directed}\}.$$
On the full tangent bundle $TO$, define charged transport as the vector field
whose integral curves, with parameter $\lambda=s_m/M$, satisfy
$$\frac{dx^a}{d\lambda}=P^a,\qquad \nabla_{dx/d\lambda}P^a=cqF^a{}_bP^b.$$
In a smooth chart its expression is
$$\mathcal L_{F,q}:=P^a\partial_{x^a}+\left(-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}P^bP^c+cqF^a{}_bP^b\right)\partial_{P^a}.$$
The restriction of this field to $\mathcal P_M^+(O)$ is justified by
[[lem-tgr-charged-liouville-preserves-mass-shell]]. For any smooth real scalar
$\zeta$ and smooth vector field $\beta$ with components in inverse joules,
define the dimensionless charged exponential ansatz on the shell by
$$f(x,P):=\exp\!\left(\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)\right),\qquad \beta_b:=g_{bc}\beta^c.$$
The equation $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$ means that the derivative of this function
along the restricted charged transport vector field vanishes.

Under a smooth gauge change $A\mapsto A+d\chi$, with $\chi$ in tesla square
metres, the corresponding compensator changes by
$\Lambda_\xi\mapsto\Lambda_\xi+\xi(\chi)$. These definitions fix the sign
convention for $F$, the Lorentz force, and the potential terms used on this
page.

In ZF, let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be smooth, and let $a\in U$. If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open neighbourhoods $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that $f|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Writing $g=(f|_V)^{-1}$,
$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$
No choice axiom is used.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim:
Fix $(x_0,P_0)$ with $C(x_0,P_0)=0$. Since $M>0$, $P_0\ne0$; by
nondegeneracy of $g_{x_0}$ there is a tangent vector $V$ with
$g_{x_0}(P_0,V)\ne0$. In any bundle chart around $(x_0,P_0)$, choose a fiber
coordinate direction $P^j$ on which this nonzero covector has a nonzero
component. The map from the eight chart coordinates to the four base
coordinates, $C$, and the other three fiber coordinates has Jacobian
determinant equal, up to sign, to $\partial C/\partial P^j=2g_{jb}P^b\ne0$.
By [F2] it is a local diffeomorphism, so $C=0$ is locally a smooth
codimension-one coordinate slice. The future timelike sheet is an open
component of this level set. The supplied tangent-bundle structure carries
[A2].

The differential of $C$ along $\mathcal L_{F,q}$ is computed using the
covariant horizontal derivative and $\nabla g=0$:
$$dC(\mathcal L_{F,q})=2g(P,cqF^\sharp(P))=2cqP^aF_{ab}P^b=0.$$
The last contraction vanishes because $P^aP^b$ is symmetric in $a,b$ while
$F_{ab}$ is antisymmetric. Thus $\mathcal L_{F,q}$ lies in the kernel of
$dC$, which is the tangent space to the regular level set from step 1.1; the
future sheet is open in that set, so the vector field is tangent there as
well. Its restriction is therefore well defined.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement uses a nonempty domain O and M>0; at every x∈O a Lorentz frame has future vectors of norm −M², so the shell fiber is nonempty.
Step 2.1 remains valid when q=0 or F=0; the electromagnetic contribution vanishes and dC of the geodesic transport field is still zero.
Step 1.1 is pointwise at an arbitrary shell point and needs only one nonzero fiber coordinate derivative.
Step 1.1 uses M>0 to exclude P=0 and nondegeneracy of g to get d_PC≠0; the massless M=0 degenerate level is outside the Statement.

boundaries.reason: The result concerns a vector field tangent to a shell, not a trajectory with endpoint conditions.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 makes one pointwise existential choice of a vector V and a nonzero coordinate direction; it does not select from a countable family.

boundaries.reason: The Statement is a direct regularity and tangency implication, not an iff claim.
The Statement is a direct regularity and tangency implication, not an iff claim.

statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex ([[def-interval]]) and let
$f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$ ([[def-continuity-real]]) and
differentiable at every point of $I$ that is interior to $I$
([[def-interior-closure-boundary-r]], [[def-derivative]]), with

$$f'(x) = 0 \qquad \text{at every interior point } x \text{ of } I .$$

Then $f$ is constant on $I$: there is a real $k$ with $f(x) = k$ for every
$x \in I$.

Consequently, if $f, g : I \to \mathbb{R}$ are both continuous on $I$ and both
differentiable at every interior point of $I$, with $f'(x) = g'(x)$ at every
interior point $x$, then there is a real $k$ with

$$f(x) \;=\; g(x) + k \qquad \text{for every } x \in I .$$

**Order-convexity of $I$ is essential and is not a convenience.** The
conclusion is false on a domain that falls into separate pieces, since a
function may be constant on each piece with different constants; nothing in the
proof would survive, because the mean value theorem is applied to the segment
joining two points of the domain and that segment must lie in the domain.

**The hypothesis is imposed only at interior points.** At an endpoint of $I$
nothing is asked at all: $f$ need not be differentiable there, and the proof
never evaluates a difference quotient at an endpoint, since it applies the mean
value theorem on a segment $[u,v] \subseteq I$ and uses the derivative only at
points of $(u,v)$, all of which are interior to $I$. What is *not* meant is that
the derivative at an endpoint is free to be nonzero: once $f$ is known to be
constant its difference quotient at an endpoint is constantly $0$, so wherever
$f'$ exists at an endpoint it is $0$ too. That is a consequence of the theorem,
not a hypothesis of it.

derivations.claim: In any coordinate chart, $(\iota_\xi F)_a=\xi^b(\partial_bA_a-\partial_aA_b)$ and $d(\iota_\xi A)_a=\partial_a(\xi^bA_b)$. Adding these identities gives $(\iota_\xi F)_a+d(\iota_\xi A)_a=\xi^b\partial_bA_a+A_b\partial_a\xi^b=(\mathcal L_\xi A)_a$. Using $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$ and [F1], this yields $\iota_\xi F=d\Lambda_\xi-d(\iota_\xi A)=-d\Psi_\xi$.

Metric compatibility and $P=Mw$ yield
$$\frac{d}{ds_m}g(P,\xi) =cq\,g(F^\sharp(w),\xi)+M w^a w^b\nabla_b\xi_a =cq\,(\iota_\xi F)(w) =-cq\,w(\Psi_\xi).$$
The middle Killing term vanishes because $w^aw^b$ is symmetric and
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$; the force contraction has the displayed sign since
$g(F^\sharp(w),\xi)=\xi^cF_{cb}w^b$.

Since $d\Psi_\xi/ds_m=w(\Psi_\xi)$ and $q\Phi_\xi=-cq\Psi_\xi$,
$$\frac{dH_\xi}{ds_m} =-\frac{d}{ds_m}g(P,\xi)-cq\,w(\Psi_\xi) =0.$$
The curve is $C^2$ and the fields are smooth, so $H_\xi$ is $C^1$ and hence
continuous on $J$. Its derivative is zero by step 2.1; since the open interval
$J$ is order-convex, [F3] makes $H_\xi$ constant there.

Under $A'=A+d\chi$, $dA'=F$ because the coordinate mixed partials of the smooth scalar $\chi$ commute. Also $(\mathcal L_\xi d\chi)_a=\xi^b\partial_b\partial_a\chi+(\partial_a\xi^b)\partial_b\chi=\partial_a(\xi^b\partial_b\chi)$, so $\Lambda'_\xi:=\Lambda_\xi+\xi(\chi)$ satisfies $\mathcal L_\xi A'=d\Lambda'_\xi$. Since $(\iota_\xi d\chi)=\xi(\chi)$, $\Psi'_\xi=\Psi_\xi$ and $H'_\xi=H_\xi$. Replacing $\Lambda_\xi$ by $\Lambda_\xi+C_0/c$ leaves $d\Lambda_\xi$ fixed and sends $\Phi_\xi$ to $\Phi_\xi+C_0$, so $H_\xi$ changes by $qC_0$.

For the smooth Lorentzian data, $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, $F=dA$, and charged
transport vector field defined in [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]], the set

Use the Lorentzian geometry, units, charge sign, potential $A$, field $F=dA$,
compensator $\Lambda_\xi$, and $C^2$ charged trajectory $x(s_m)$ of
[[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]]. Assume the global potential symmetry
$\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Define
$$H_\xi:=-g(P,\xi)+q\Phi_\xi=-g(P,\xi)-cq\Psi_\xi.$$
Then $\iota_\xi F=-d\Psi_\xi$, and $H_\xi$ is constant along every interval
on which the trajectory obeys the stated Lorentz equation. It is invariant under
$A\mapsto A+d\chi$, $\Lambda_\xi\mapsto\Lambda_\xi+\xi(\chi)$. Replacing the

This is a conditional mathematical statement about curves satisfying the
displayed equation. It asserts neither existence of such curves for arbitrary
initial data nor that the model describes nature.

Let $O$ and the smooth fields $(g,\nabla,\xi,T,u,N_\xi,\beta)$ be as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then
$$\beta\text{ is Killing}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\xi T=T_K\text{ for a constant }T_K>0.$$
When this holds, $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$, and the Killing congruence has
$$\xi(N_\xi)=0,\qquad a=\nabla\log N_\xi,\qquad \theta=0,\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0.$$
If $\xi$ is replaced by $b\xi$ with a constant $b>0$, then
$N_\xi$ and $T_K$ scale by $b$, while $u$ and $\beta$ are unchanged.

Let $(V,g,C^+)$ be a four-dimensional time-oriented Lorentz vector space of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with future cone $C^+$ as in
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]. Let $M>0$ and let $A$ be a
symmetric bilinear form on $V$ and $b$ a covector. If
$$A(P,P)+b(P)=0\qquad\text{for every }P\in C^+\text{ with }g(P,P)=-M^2,$$
then $A=0$ and $b=0$. If instead this identity holds for every nonzero future
null vector $P\in\overline{C^+}$, then $b=0$ and $A=\lambda g$ for some
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$. The second clause is the exact massless conformal
exception.
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be convex and open. If $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ is totally differentiable at every point and $Df(z)=0$ for every $z\in U$, then $f$ is constant on $U$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim:
Since $f>0$, $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$ is equivalent to
$\mathcal L_{F,q}(\zeta+g(\beta,P))=0$. In a chart, the connection term in the
vertical part of $\mathcal L_{F,q}$ combines with
$P^a\partial_a\beta_b$ to give $P^aP^b\nabla_a\beta_b$; its electromagnetic
part gives $cq\beta^aF_{ab}P^b$. Thus on the future shell
$$\frac{\mathcal L_{F,q}f}{f} =P^aP^b\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)} +P^b\bigl(\nabla_b\zeta+cq\beta^aF_{ab}\bigr).$$
The stationarity equation sets this quadratic-plus-linear expression to zero
for every future massive shell vector.

If $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$, apply [F5] pointwise to
$A_{ab}:=\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}$ and
$b_b:=\nabla_b\zeta+cq\beta^aF_{ab}$. It gives
$\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0$ and
$d\zeta=-cq\,\iota_\beta F$. Conversely these equations make both terms in
the expression of step 1.1 vanish for every shell vector, so
$\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$. This proves the first equivalence using the exact massive-shell clause of [F5].

Now impose the additional global condition [A2]. In the stationary setting
$\beta=u/(k_BT)$ is collinear with $\xi$.
When the first condition holds, the thermal-normalization interface [F4] gives a
constant $T_K>0$ with
$NT=T_K$ and $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$. By [F3],
$\iota_\xi F=-d\Psi_\xi$ and $\Phi_\xi=-c\Psi_\xi$, hence
$\iota_\xi F=d\Phi_\xi/c$. Substitution into the second condition gives
$$d\zeta=-cq\,\iota_\beta F =-\frac{cq}{k_BT_K}\,\iota_\xi F =-\frac{q}{k_BT_K}\,d\Phi_\xi.$$
Therefore $d(\zeta+q\Phi_\xi/(k_BT_K))=0$.

Conversely, under [A2], suppose the three displayed redshift equations
hold. Then
$\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$ is Killing since $T_K$ is constant and $\xi$ is Killing.
Also $\zeta+q\Phi_\xi/(k_BT_K)=\mu_K/(k_BT_K)$ is constant, so
$d\zeta=-q\,d\Phi_\xi/(k_BT_K)=-cq\,\iota_\beta F$ by [F3]. Step 2.1 then
gives $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$.

Around every point choose a chart whose image contains a convex open ball.
The chain rule and
$d(\zeta+q\Phi_\xi/(k_BT_K))=0$ give zero total derivative for the coordinate
representative on that ball, so [F6] makes it
constant there. It is therefore locally constant on $O$. The level set of
this function through any chosen point is nonempty and open, and its
complement is also open because the function is locally constant. Connectedness
of $O$ forces that level set to be all of $O$. Write its constant value as
$\mu_K/(k_BT_K)$. Multiplying
$\zeta+q\Phi_\xi/(k_BT_K)=\mu_K/(k_BT_K)$ by $k_BT_K=k_BNT$ yields
$N\mu+q\Phi_\xi=\mu_K$.

Finally [F3] gives $H_\xi=-g(P,\xi)+q\Phi_\xi$. Since
$\xi=Nu$ and $E_{\rm loc}=-g(P,u)$, $-g(P,\xi)=NE_{\rm loc}$. Using
$NT=T_K$ and $N\mu+q\Phi_\xi=\mu_K$,
$$-\frac{H_\xi-\mu_K}{k_BT_K} =-\frac{NE_{\rm loc}+q\Phi_\xi-\mu_K}{k_BNT} =-\frac{E_{\rm loc}-\mu}{k_BT} =\zeta+g(\beta,P).$$
This is an algebraic equality of dimensionless exponents; it asserts no
statistical preparation or normalization.

citations.quote:
Use SI dimensions and the signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Take the geometric data of
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]: $O$ is a nonempty connected open domain in a
smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$, $\nabla$ is the
Levi–Civita connection, and $\xi$ is a smooth future-directed timelike Killing
field with dimensionless components in physical length coordinates $x^0=ct$
and $x^i$ measured in metres. Put $N:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and
$u:=\xi/N$, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its smooth
tangent-bundle data carry the supplier's explicit foundational assumption
[[def-countable-choice]] ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$); no stronger choice principle
is added here.

For a smooth real one-form $A$ on $O$, define the electromagnetic two-form by
$$F_{ab}:=(dA)_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a.$$
Here $A_a$ has units tesla metres and $F_{ab}$ has units tesla. A global gauge
compensator is a smooth real function $\Lambda_\xi$ on $O$ satisfying
$$(\mathcal L_\xi A)_a:=\xi^b\partial_bA_a+A_b\partial_a\xi^b =\partial_a\Lambda_\xi.$$
The units of $\Lambda_\xi$ are tesla metres. Define contraction by
$(\iota_\xi F)_a:=\xi^bF_{ba}$ and set
$$\Psi_\xi:=\xi^aA_a-\Lambda_\xi,\qquad \Phi_\xi:=-c\Psi_\xi.$$
Thus $\Psi_\xi$ has units tesla metres and $\Phi_\xi$ has units volts.

Let $c>0$ be the speed of light, let $m>0$ be a particle rest mass in
kilograms, let $q\in\mathbb R$ be its charge in coulombs, and put
$M:=mc^2>0$ joules. A charged massive Lorentz trajectory is a $C^2$ curve
$x:J\to O$, where $J$ is an open real interval, parametrized by physical
length $s_m=c\tau$ in metres, with future unit tangent
$w:=dx/ds_m$, $g(w,w)=-1$, energy four-vector $P:=Mw$, and equation
$$\nabla_wP^a=cqF^a{}_bw^b,\qquad F^a{}_b:=g^{ac}F_{cb}.$$
In particular $g(P,P)=-M^2$ and $P$ is future directed. This is a conditional
definition of curves satisfying the equation; it makes no existence claim.

The future massive shell for this definition is the subset
$$\mathcal P_M^+(O):=\{(x,P)\in TO:g_x(P,P)=-M^2,\ P\text{ future directed}\}.$$
On the full tangent bundle $TO$, define charged transport as the vector field
whose integral curves, with parameter $\lambda=s_m/M$, satisfy
$$\frac{dx^a}{d\lambda}=P^a,\qquad \nabla_{dx/d\lambda}P^a=cqF^a{}_bP^b.$$
In a smooth chart its expression is
$$\mathcal L_{F,q}:=P^a\partial_{x^a}+\left(-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}P^bP^c+cqF^a{}_bP^b\right)\partial_{P^a}.$$
The restriction of this field to $\mathcal P_M^+(O)$ is justified by
[[lem-tgr-charged-liouville-preserves-mass-shell]]. For any smooth real scalar
$\zeta$ and smooth vector field $\beta$ with components in inverse joules,
define the dimensionless charged exponential ansatz on the shell by
$$f(x,P):=\exp\!\left(\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)\right),\qquad \beta_b:=g_{bc}\beta^c.$$
The equation $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$ means that the derivative of this function
along the restricted charged transport vector field vanishes.

Under a smooth gauge change $A\mapsto A+d\chi$, with $\chi$ in tesla square
metres, the corresponding compensator changes by
$\Lambda_\xi\mapsto\Lambda_\xi+\xi(\chi)$. These definitions fix the sign
convention for $F$, the Lorentz force, and the potential terms used on this
page.

Let $O$ be a connected domain with the stationary Lorentzian data, potential
$A$, field $F=dA$, Killing field $\xi$, lapse $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$, future
unit stationary observer $u=\xi/N$, and charged transport on the future mass
shell from [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]]. Let $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$,
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$ for a smooth proper-temperature scalar $T:O\to(0,\infty)$,
and $\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$ for a smooth chemical-potential scalar
$\mu:O\to\mathbb R$. Define $f(x,P)=\exp(\zeta+g(\beta,P))$. Without any global
potential-symmetry assumption,
$$\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \beta\text{ is Killing and }d\zeta=-cq\,\iota_\beta F.$$

If, in addition, a global smooth compensator satisfies
$\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$, define $\Phi_\xi=-c(\iota_\xi A-\Lambda_\xi)$.
Then the stationarity conditions above are equivalent to the existence of
constants $T_K>0$ and $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$NT=T_K,\qquad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K},\qquad N\mu+q\Phi_\xi=\mu_K.$$
With $E_{\rm loc}:=-g(P,u)$ and
$H_\xi:=-g(P,\xi)+q\Phi_\xi$, the same exponent then has both forms
$$\zeta+g(\beta,P)=-\frac{E_{\rm loc}-\mu}{k_BT} =-\frac{H_\xi-\mu_K}{k_BT_K}.$$
Here $N$ is dimensionless, $T,T_K$ are kelvins, $\mu,\mu_K,E_{\rm loc},H_\xi$
are joules per particle, $\Phi_\xi$ is volts, $q$ is coulombs, and
$\beta\cdot P$ and $\zeta$ are dimensionless. All claims are mathematical
conditional deductions from the displayed smooth data; no equilibrium state,
particle ensemble, or physical realization is asserted to exist.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The product metric is smooth, has signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and is invariant under translations of $x^0$; hence $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$ is a future timelike Killing field and $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}=1$. The form $\vartheta$ is globally defined, closed, and independent of $x^0$, so $A=E_0x^0\vartheta$ is a global one-form and differentiation gives $F=dA=E_0dx^0\wedge\vartheta$. Since $\mathcal L_\xi dx^0=d(\xi(x^0))=d1=0$ and $\mathcal L_\xi\vartheta=0$, the product rule gives $\mathcal L_\xi F=0$; direct contraction gives $\iota_\xi F=E_0\vartheta$.

The product rule gives $\mathcal L_\xi A=E_0\xi(x^0)\vartheta+E_0x^0\mathcal L_\xi\vartheta=E_0\vartheta$, whose period around the circle is $E_0L\ne0$. Every exact one-form $d\Lambda$ for a global smooth real $\Lambda$ has zero integral around this closed circle, since its line integral is the endpoint difference of $\Lambda$. Thus no global $\Lambda_\xi$ satisfies $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Under a gauge change $A\mapsto A+d\chi$, the coordinate formula gives $(\mathcal L_\xi d\chi)_a=\xi^b\partial_b\partial_a\chi+(\partial_a\xi^b)\partial_b\chi=\partial_a(\xi^b\partial_b\chi)$; this is exact and has zero circle period. Hence the nonzero period cannot be removed by a single-valued gauge.

Here $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$ is Killing. If a global smooth $\zeta$ made $f$ from [F1] stationary, [F2] would give
$$d\zeta=-cq\,\iota_\beta F =-\frac{cqE_0}{k_BT_K}\vartheta.$$
Integrating around the positive circle gives $0=\oint d\zeta=-cqE_0L/(k_BT_K)$, which contradicts $qE_0\ne0$ and $T_K>0$. Hence no single-valued global $\zeta$ exists.

Step 2.1 uses only the forward implication of the theorem: stationarity would force dζ=−cq i_βF.
